title: Chapter 9 Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of the box model, sizing, spacing, borders, and box‑sizing!

questions.question: What are the four layers of the CSS box model, from inside out?
questions.explanation: Content is innermost, then padding, then border, then margin.

questions.question: By default (`content-box`), the `width` property sets the width of which area?
questions.explanation: In `content-box`, `width` = content area; padding and border are extra.

questions.question: If `width: 200px; padding: 20px; border: 5px solid;` with `content-box`, total rendered width is?
questions.explanation: 200 + 20+20 (padding) + 5+5 (border) = 250px.

questions.question: Which property prevents an element from becoming wider than 800px?
questions.explanation: `max-width` sets the upper limit.

questions.question: What does `height: 100%;` do if the parent has `height: auto;`?
options: Makes the element as tall as the viewport
Makes the element 100% of the parent's content height (which might be auto, so often 0)
questions.explanation: Percentage height needs a parent with explicit height; with auto, it behaves as auto unless content dictates.

questions.question: Which shorthand value for `padding` sets top=10, right=20, bottom=30, left=20?
questions.explanation: Three values: top, right & left, bottom. So right and left become 20px.

questions.question: Margins that share the same vertical space and combine into one are said to ______.
questions.explanation: Margin collapse means adjacent vertical margins merge into the largest one.

questions.question: Negative margins are allowed in CSS.
questions.explanation: Negative margins pull elements closer or make them overlap; they're valid.

questions.question: How do you centre a block‑level element horizontally with a fixed width?
questions.explanation: `margin: 0 auto;` sets left/right margins to auto, centering the block.

questions.question: What is required for a `border` to be visible?
questions.explanation: `border-style` must be set (and not `none`) for the border to appear.

questions.question: Which property makes an element's corners rounded?
questions.explanation: `border-radius` controls the curvature of corners.

questions.question: What does `border-radius: 50%;` on a square element create?
questions.explanation: 50% on a square makes a circle.

questions.question: What is the key difference between `outline` and `border`?
options: Outline does not affect layout (no space taken)
questions.explanation: Outline is drawn over the content without increasing element size; border affects layout.

questions.question: Which property is commonly used to give focus indicators to keyboard users?
questions.explanation: Browsers apply `outline` on focused elements by default.

questions.question: What does `box-sizing: border-box;` do?
options: Makes width/height include padding and border
Removes the border from the box model
questions.explanation: `border-box` includes padding and border in the specified width/height.

questions.question: With `box-sizing: border-box; width: 400px; padding: 15px; border: 10px;`, what is the actual content width?
questions.explanation: 400 - (15*2) padding - (10*2) border = 350px.

questions.question: Why is the universal `*, *::before, *::after { box-sizing: border-box; }` so popular?
options: It makes sizing intuitive and prevents overflow issues
questions.explanation: `border-box` makes the box model easier to reason about, especially in responsive layouts.

questions.question: `padding` values can be negative.
questions.explanation: Padding cannot be negative; negative margins are allowed.

questions.question: Which property controls what happens when content overflows an element's box?
questions.explanation: `overflow` handles content that's too big (hidden, scroll, auto, visible).

questions.question: What is the effect of `margin: 10px auto;`?
options: Sets top/bottom margin 10px, left/right auto (centers horizontally if width set)
questions.explanation: Two values: top/bottom, left/right. Auto on left/right centers block elements.

questions.question: What is the default `box-sizing` value?
questions.explanation: The initial value is `content-box`.

questions.question: Which of these is a valid border style?
questions.explanation: `double` is a valid style; `inset`, `outset`, `groove`, `ridge` also exist, but 'raised' is not.

questions.question: How can you prevent margin collapse between a parent and its first child?
options: Add `padding-top: 1px;` or `border-top: 1px solid transparent;` to the parent
questions.explanation: Both adding a border/padding or using flex on the parent can block margin collapse.
